sources.title: Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī, Hadith 3507
sources.citation: Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī, Chapters on Supplication, Hadith 3507, through al-Walīd ibn Muslim from Shuʿayb ibn Abī Ḥamza. At-Tirmidhī calls it gharīb and Darussalam grades it daʿīf. Hadith scholars consider the list of Names most likely a narrator's compilation rather than the Prophet's own words (Ibn Ḥajar, Fatḥ al-Bārī). The sunnah.com text lists ninety-eight Names after “Allah” and does not include al-Aḥad; this app's ninety-nine include al-Aḥad, as in al-Khaṭṭābī's commentary on the same list.
sources.usedFor: The traditional list and order of the Names this app follows, adapted as described in this citation (not an identical reproduction of this hadith's text).

sources.title: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Hadith 6410
sources.citation: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Book of Invocations, Hadith 6410: “Allah has ninety-nine Names, one hundred less one…”. The narration does not list the Names.
sources.usedFor: The authentic statement that Allah has ninety-nine Names.

sources.title: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Hadith 2677a
sources.citation: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Book of Remembrance and Supplication, Hadith 2677a: “There are ninety-nine Names of Allah; whoever preserves them will enter Paradise.” The narration does not list the Names.
sources.usedFor: The authentic statement that Allah has ninety-nine Names.

sources.title: The Qurʾān
sources.citation: Arabic text as published by the Tanzil project (Uthmani script, the reading of Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim). The verses for each Name are recorded in the content audit.
sources.usedFor: Where the Name, or the attribute it names, occurs in the Qurʾān.

sources.title: al-Khaṭṭābī, Shaʾn al-Duʿāʾ
sources.citation: Abū Sulaymān Ḥamd ibn Muḥammad al-Khaṭṭābī (d. 388 AH), Shaʾn al-Duʿāʾ, which explains each Name of this list in order. Consulted in the al-Maktaba al-Shāmila edition.
sources.usedFor: Cross-checking the list and its order, and the classical meaning of each Name.

sources.title: Ibn Ḥajar, Fatḥ al-Bārī
sources.citation: Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī, Fatḥ al-Bārī, commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6410, vol. 11, pp. 219–221 (Islamweb edition): the authenticity of the listed Names and the differences between their narrations.
sources.usedFor: The scholarly assessment of the list and of Names whose inclusion is disputed.

sources.title: Ibn al-Qayyim, Badāʾiʿ al-Fawāʾid
sources.citation: Ibn al-Qayyim, Badāʾiʿ al-Fawāʾid, on Names that are only mentioned together with their counterpart, as excerpted by Ibn ʿUthaymīn in al-Muntaqā min Farāʾid al-Fawāʾid.
sources.usedFor: Names that should be mentioned together with their counterpart.

sources.title: al-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-Bayān
sources.citation: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-Bayān (Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī), consulted on quran.com for al-Ḥashr 59:23 and al-Qamar 54:42.
sources.usedFor: The classical meaning of Names whose English rendering needs care.

sources.title: Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī, Hadith 1314
sources.citation: Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī, Hadith 1314: “Indeed Allah is al-Musaʿʿir, al-Qābiḍ, al-Bāsiṭ, ar-Razzāq.” At-Tirmidhī: ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ. Darussalam: ṣaḥīḥ.
sources.usedFor: Al-Qābiḍ, al-Bāsiṭ and ar-Razzāq named in an authentic hadith.

sources.title: Sunan Abī Dāwūd, Hadith 4955
sources.citation: Sunan Abī Dāwūd, Hadith 4955: “Allah is al-Ḥakam, and to Him belongs judgment.” Al-Albānī: ṣaḥīḥ.
sources.usedFor: Al-Ḥakam named in an authentic hadith.

sources.title: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Hadith 1120
sources.citation: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Hadith 1120, the Prophet's night prayer supplication: “You are the Light of the heavens and the earth… You are al-Muqaddim and You are al-Muʾakhkhir.”
sources.usedFor: Al-Muqaddim, al-Muʾakhkhir and an-Nūr in an authentic supplication.

sources.title: Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī, Hadith 3475
sources.citation: Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī, Hadith 3475: “O Allah, I ask You… You are Allah, there is no god but You, al-Aḥad, aṣ-Ṣamad.” Darussalam: ṣaḥīḥ.
sources.usedFor: Al-Aḥad and aṣ-Ṣamad in an authentic supplication.

sources.title: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Hadith 7378
sources.citation: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Hadith 7378: “No one is more patient with hurtful words He hears than Allah.”
sources.usedFor: Allah's patience established in an authentic hadith.

sources.title: Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī, Hadith 2516
sources.citation: Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī, Hadith 2516: if all people gathered to benefit or harm you, they could do so only with what Allah has written. At-Tirmidhī: ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
sources.usedFor: That benefit and harm come only by Allah's decree.
